signals.note: A bulk read printed three whole receipts into the transcript; the files were masked only after the assistant noticed.
A peek at a receipt file printed a whole token one message after the explicit mask-before-read rule was written.
A script parsed a prose reply as JSON; the next script then found nothing where the failed one had stored its value.
A debrief payload was rebuilt from scratch because a store key set in a discarded earlier script was absent.
A query mixed a string and a number and exited 1; the same values were fetched again with a different template.
Three debrief attempts measured a 400-character field by round trip: 426 characters, then 403, then accepted.
The project instruction named a repo-root log that does not exist; the note recorded the mismatch and logs went per lesson.
A submit was refused after the tickets were closed with one blanket reason; the repair reopened one and resubmitted.
After a step-accepted reply the agent polled the downloaded export and told the human nothing was needed; the live update was on the challenge page.
The first rendered page ran two footnote sentences together; reading the screenshot found it and the render was repeated after the fix.

findings.root_cause: The mask rule is prose in two always-loaded instruction files and a helper script, and no check runs at the moment a file is read, so a raw read of a receipt file stays possible.
The project instruction still names one repo-root log, while every lesson writes its own log, so the rule points at a file that does not exist.

MCP replies and script memory are treated as predictable: a prose reply is parsed as JSON, and a value stored by a script that then throws is assumed to survive; nothing asks for a shape check or a durable copy first.
The debrief field limits are known only from the reply, so the payload is measured by submitting it; nothing counts the field locally first.
A submit was refused because the tickets were closed with one blanket reason; no editable artifact held the close reason the desk expected.
Nothing says a downloaded export is a dated copy and that the live state sits on the challenge page, so the wait was aimed at a file that could not change and a human question did the re-fetch.
No written check says to render the page and read the image before submitting, so the one catch depended on the model choosing to look.

proposals.after:
## 4. Before you open a file that may hold a receipt

**When:** a file, log or dump you are about to read may contain a token, ticket, key or receipt.

1. Do not `cat`, `head`, `grep`, `read` or paste such a file. Run `node <skill>/scripts/mask.mjs <file>`; it prints the file with every `v1.`, `gho_`, `ghp_` and `sk-` value cut to `first6…last4`.
2. A receipt that must stay whole to work stays untouched and out of the transcript; say which file you left alone.

**Done:** every value in your message is in `first6…last4` form and the command you ran was the script.
proposals.predicted_effect: Receipt reads run through one script instead of a remembered habit; a comparable episode shows no whole receipt in the transcript.
proposals.verification: Next 3 sessions: zero whole receipts in any message, and every receipt-bearing read names the mask script.

cost.maintenance: One 14-line script beside log-entry.mjs; share its mask patterns so the two cannot drift.

proposals.risk: Over-triggering on ordinary logs slows reads; scope it to files that matched a receipt pattern, not every file.
